##initializing r file from GSS
library(foreign)
  read.dct <- function(dct, labels.included = "yes") {
      temp <- readLines(dct)
      temp <- temp[grepl("_column", temp)]
      switch(labels.included,
             yes = {
                 pattern <- "_column\\(([0-9]+)\\)\\s+([a-z0-9]+)\\s+(.*)\\s+%([0-9]+)[a-z]\\s+(.*)"
                 classes <- c("numeric", "character", "character", "numeric", "character")
                 N <- 5
                 NAMES <- c("StartPos", "Str", "ColName", "ColWidth", "ColLabel")
             },
             no = {
                 pattern <- "_column\\(([0-9]+)\\)\\s+([a-z0-9]+)\\s+(.*)\\s+%([0-9]+).*"
                 classes <- c("numeric", "character", "character", "numeric")
                 N <- 4
                 NAMES <- c("StartPos", "Str", "ColName", "ColWidth")
             })
      temp_metadata <- setNames(lapply(1:N, function(x) {
          out <- gsub(pattern, paste("\\", x, sep = ""), temp)
          out <- gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$", "", out)
          out <- gsub('\"', "", out, fixed = TRUE)
          class(out) <- classes[x] ; out }), NAMES)
      temp_metadata[["ColName"]] <- make.names(gsub("\\s", "", temp_metadata[["ColName"]]))
      temp_metadata
  }

  read.dat <- function(dat, metadata_var, labels.included = "yes") {
      read.table(dat, col.names = metadata_var[["ColName"]])
  }

#Part 3: Correlation Tests 
##Part 3A: Conservative Variables Correlation
##creating scatterplots to view relationships between certain variables and conservatives
variables <- c("LIBHOMO","GUNLAW", "PRAYER", "FEPOL", "ABANY", "HOMOSEX", "SEXEDUC")

##creating a pivot table
long_table <- conservative %>%
  select(POLVIEWS, all_of(variables)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(variables),
               names_to = "Views",
               values_to = "Responses") %>%
  mutate(PoliticalViews = case_when(
    Views == "LIBHOMO" ~ "Gay Books in Library",
    Views == "GUNLAW" ~ "In Favor of Gun Control",
    Views == "PRAYER" ~ "Prayer in Schools",
    Views == "FEPOL" ~ "Females in Politics",
    Views == "ABANY" ~ "Abortion for any Reason",
    Views == "HOMOSEX" ~ "Same Sex Relationships",
    Views == "SEXEDUC" ~ "Sex Education in Schools"
  ))

###scatterplot matrix
ggplot(long_table, aes(x = Responses, y = Views)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkred", alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~PoliticalViews, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Conservative Responses to American Societal Issues",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Views") +
  theme_minimal()

###correlations and derivative metrics
variables_to_exclude <- c("-100", "-99", "-98", "-97", "1", "2", "3", "4")

new_white <- white %>% 
  filter(!PARTYID %in% variables_to_exclude) 
###denomination
cor.test(new_white$LIBHOMO, new_white$DENOM, method = "kendall")
## 
##  Kendall's rank correlation tau
## 
## data:  new_white$LIBHOMO and new_white$DENOM
## z = -0.28532, p-value = 0.7754
## alternative hypothesis: true tau is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:

###heatmap
long_matrix <- matrix %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Var1, names_to = "Var2", values_to = "Correlation")

### create a heatmap
ggplot(long_matrix, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "darkred", mid = "white", high = "darkblue",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)), size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Heatmap",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

##Part 4: t-tests
## see if liberals and conservatives are normally distributed among denomination
##filtering out "not applicable"  and "did not answer" responses first
values_to_exclude <- c("-100", "-99", "-98", "-97")


new_conservative <- conservative %>% 
  filter(!DENOM %in% values_to_exclude) 

new_liberal <- liberal %>% 
  filter(!DENOM %in% values_to_exclude) 

#now doing histograms with only respondents who chose a denomination
hist(new_conservative$DENOM, breaks = 100, main = "Conservatives' Denominations", 
     ylab = "Political View", xlab = "Denominations")
hist(new_liberal$DENOM, breaks = 100, main = "Liberals' Denominations", 
     ylab = "Political View", xlab = "Denominations", add = TRUE, col = "red")

mean(new_conservative$DENOM)
## [1] 4.220831
median(new_conservative$DENOM)
## [1] 4
mean(new_liberal$DENOM)
## [1] 4.449772
median(new_liberal$DENOM)
## [1] 5
#variance
var(new_conservative$DENOM)
## [1] 6.185371
var(new_liberal$DENOM)
## [1] 4.646213
var(new_conservative$PARTYID)
## [1] 44.41609
var(new_liberal$PARTYID)
## [1] 25.52293
var(new_conservative$SEX)
## [1] 20.33477
var(new_liberal$SEX)
## [1] 23.35392
## t-tests
t.test(x = new_conservative$DENOM,       # group 1 sample mean
       y = new_liberal$DENOM,     # group 2 sample mean
       alternative = "two.sided",  # one or two sided test
       mu = 0,                     # hypothesized difference between the means
       paired = FALSE, 
       var.equal = FALSE,          # since variances are not equal (per above), use this option
       conf.level = .95)           # desired level of confidence
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  new_conservative$DENOM and new_liberal$DENOM
## t = -1.8892, df = 803.3, p-value = 0.05922
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.466812546  0.008930341
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
##  4.220831  4.449772
t.test(new_conservative$PARTYID, new_liberal$PARTYID, 
       alternative = "two.sided",
       mu = 0, 
       paired = FALSE, 
       var.equal = FALSE,
       conf.level = .95)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  new_conservative$PARTYID and new_liberal$PARTYID
## t = 12.914, df = 919.55, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  3.240470 4.401863
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
## 4.7092947 0.8881279
t.test(new_conservative$SEX, new_liberal$SEX, 
       alternative = "two.sided",
       mu = 0, 
       paired = FALSE, 
       var.equal = FALSE,
       conf.level = .95)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  new_conservative$SEX and new_liberal$SEX
## t = -0.3662, df = 672.1, p-value = 0.7143
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.6017847  0.4125985
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
##  1.311800  1.406393
#ordinal logistic regression - we're modeling our outcome variable (political views)
##our main predictor is denomination and covariates will be the respondent variables above

# Evangelical denominations: Baptist (1), Other Denomination (6), Non-denominational (7)
white$evangelical <- ifelse(white$DENOM %in% c(1, 6, 7), 1, 0)

# Convert to factor
white$evangelical <- factor(white$evangelical, 
                            labels = c("Not_Evangelical", "Evangelical"))
white$POLVIEWS <- factor(white$POLVIEWS,
                         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7),
                         ordered = TRUE)

library(MASS)
## 
## Attaching package: 'MASS'
## 
## The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
## 
##     select
model <- polr(POLVIEWS ~ evangelical + ABANY + GUNLAW + PRAYER +
                HOMOSEX + FEPOL + SEXEDUC + YEAR,
              data = white, 
              Hess = TRUE)

summary(model)

## polr(formula = POLVIEWS ~ evangelical + ABANY + GUNLAW + PRAYER +

# 95% confidence intervals for the odds ratios
exp(confint(model))

ctable <- coef(summary(model))
p_values <- pnorm(abs(ctable[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
ctable <- cbind(ctable, "p value" = p_values)
ctable
